interest:
I study JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN, especially
little red dots (LRDs), compact red sources, dust-reddened or broad-line AGN,
early black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.

Prioritize papers about:
1. JWST/NIRCam/NIRSpec/MIRI observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN
2. little red dots, compact red galaxies, obscured AGN, broad-line AGN, and
   high-redshift black hole candidates
3. SED fitting, spectroscopy, emission lines, photometric redshifts, stellar
   masses, dust attenuation, AGN contamination, and source classification
4. high-redshift galaxy formation, reionization-era galaxies, early SMBH
   growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution
5. survey papers from CEERS, JADES, UNCOVER, COSMOS-Web, PRIMER, GLASS,
   RUBIES, and similar JWST deep fields

Also keep papers about AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs),
large multimodal models (LMMs), foundation models, anomaly detection,
automated classification, spectral/photometric inference, or research agents
when they are applied to astronomy, astrophysics, JWST data, galaxy surveys,
AGN selection, or literature/data analysis.

Deprioritize unrelated stellar, solar-system, local-universe, gravitational
wave, or purely theoretical papers unless they directly inform high-redshift
galaxies, AGN, JWST analysis, or AI-for-astronomy workflows.

papers.title: A dense, metal-rich absorber driven by a heavily dust-obscured galaxy: The direct evidence of CGM enrichment at $z\sim7$
papers.authors: Qinyue Fei , Seiji Fujimoto , Gabriel Brammer , Lise Christensen , Marianne Vestergaard , Rohan P. Naidu , Robert A. Simcoe , Norman Murray , Luis C. Ho , Ruancun Li , Volker Bromm , Javier Álvarez-Márquez , Hollis B. Akins , Yoshihisa Asada , Simona Di Stefano , Kohei Inayoshi , Vasily Kokorev , Jorryt Matthee , Romain A. Meyer , Ava Polzin , Francesco Valentino , Fabian Walter , Marcel Neeleman , Fengwu Sun , Yunjing Wu , Mengyuan Xiao
papers.abstract: We report the serendipitous discovery of a dense, metal-enriched circumgalactic medium (CGM) absorber at z=7.03, together with its host galaxy, identified along the sightline toward a red quasar. The absorber exhibits the largest rest-frame equivalent widths and column densities observed to date at z>5, tracing a metal-enriched gaseous halo. Using deep JWST/NIRSpec and NOEMA observations, we characterize the absorber's physical properties and identify its host, ND1, as a vigorously star-forming galaxy at an exceptionally close impact parameter of ~16kpc, so heavily dust-obscured that it is detected only in the longest-wavelength NIRCam bands. Detections of [OIII]$\lambda$5007, H$\alpha$, and [CII]$\lambda 158\,\mu$m emission anchor the systemic redshift to z~7.0321, revealing a coherent ~50km/s blueshift of the absorbing gas relative to the host, suggesting outflow-driven metal transport into the halo. The outflow velocity, combined with the measured column density, implies an outflow rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm out}=64 M_\odot\,yr^{-1}$ and a mass loading factor $\eta=3$, indicating an energetic, chemically-enriched wind launched from a dust-obscured starburst. While the overall ionization state and [Mg/Fe] ratio align with empirical cosmic evolutionary trends, the absorber displays an enhanced carbon-to-oxygen ([C/O]) ratio. This abundance pattern suggests the nucleosynthetic yields of Population~III stellar explosions, and aligns with the host's star-formation history extending to $z \gtrsim 8$, potentially offering a rare fossil record of primordial metal enrichment. Our findings demonstrate that intense star-formation feedback can rapidly and efficiently pollute the CGM/IGM well into the Epoch of Reionization. The NIR-dark nature of the host further implies that rest-UV surveys may systematically miss the dusty sources that drive CGM- and IGM-scale metal enrichment in the early Universe.
papers.Reasons for match: This is a JWST/NIRSpec and NOEMA study of a dust-obscured galaxy at z~7 with a metal-rich CGM absorber, directly relevant to high-z dusty sources, outflows, and early enrichment.
papers.Short digest: The paper reports a dense, metal-enriched CGM absorber at z=7.03 associated with a heavily dust-obscured host galaxy ND1 detected only in the longest-wavelength NIRCam bands. NIRSpec and NOEMA spectroscopy anchor the redshift and reveal a ~50 km/s blueshifted outflow with mass loading factor eta=3 and an enhanced [C/O] ratio possibly from Population III yields. This matters for my work because it shows rest-UV surveys miss dusty sources driving early CGM/IGM enrichment, directly relevant to LRD and dust-reddened AGN/galaxy classification.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the NIRSpec emission-line measurements ([OIII], Halpha) and absorber column densities/equivalent widths
Check the NIRCam photometry and how the NIR-dark nature of the host is established
Examine the outflow rate and mass-loading derivation and the [C/O] abundance interpretation
Assess the implications for rest-UV survey incompleteness of dusty high-z sources

papers.title: On the clumpy nature of super-early galaxies
papers.authors: A. Ferrara , B. Das , M. Kohandel , A. Pallottini , E. Ntormousi
papers.abstract: JWST has revealed that galaxies during the Epoch of Reionization are composed of compact stellar clumps spanning more than two orders of magnitude in mass and size. We present an analytical framework that connects the global properties of high-redshift galactic disks to the formation, dynamical evolution and visibility of these systems. Starting from the classical Toomre instability, we derive analytical mass-size and surface density-size relations together with, for the first time, the intrinsic clump mass spectrum obtained by integrating over the entire unstable branch of the dispersion relation. The observed clumps are naturally reproduced for turbulent velocity dispersions $\sigma\simeq 10-80\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, while their location along the mass-size relation is determined by the compactness of the parent disk. The intrinsic spectrum extends over nearly two decades in mass, $5.5\lesssim\log(M_{\rm cl}/M_\odot)\lesssim7.3$, and is transformed by gas dynamical friction, which suppresses the high-mass tail ($t_{\rm df}\propto M_{\rm cl}^{-1}$) and reproduces the observed clump mass-function slope, $dN/dM\propto M^{-1.89}$. Supernova feedback is insufficient to clear the dense natal gas, whereas radiation pressure provides a robust clearing mechanism: Ly$\alpha$ trapping dominates in dust-poor clumps and infrared trapping takes over as they become enriched. The results provide the first self-consistent analytical framework connecting the formation, statistical properties and visibility of stellar clumps in super-early galaxies.
papers.Reasons for match: This directly addresses the clumpy nature of super-early (reionization-era) galaxies observed by JWST, relevant to high-redshift galaxy formation and compact source structure.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks how the compact stellar clumps seen by JWST in Epoch of Reionization galaxies form and evolve. It derives analytical mass-size and surface-density relations plus an intrinsic clump mass spectrum, showing turbulence and radiation pressure (not supernova feedback) govern clump visibility and clearing. This matters for my work because clumpy, compact high-z sources are central to interpreting LRD and compact-red-galaxy morphologies and SEDs.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the clump mass-size and surface-density relations and how they compare to JWST-observed clump samples
Check the radiation-pressure vs supernova-feedback clearing arguments and their observational signatures
Examine the predicted clump mass-function slope and whether it matches observed high-z clump statistics
Assess whether the framework makes predictions testable with NIRCam/NIRSpec imaging and spectroscopy

papers.title: JADES: Dynamical Measurements of Dark Matter Halo Masses at $z \approx 7$ Using Galaxy Pairs
papers.authors: Zihao Wu , Daniel J. Eisenstein , Benjamin D. Johnson , Lars Hernquist , Sandro Tacchella , Brant E. Robertson , Santiago Arribas , Andrew J. Bunker , Qiao Duan , Jakob M. Helton , Zhiyuan Ji , Dávid Puskás , Pierluigi Rinaldi , Fengwu Sun , Hannah Übler , Yongda Zhu
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)
papers.abstract: We present dynamical measurements of dark matter halo masses at $z\approx7$ using galaxy pairs. Galaxy pairs in the early Universe are usually in their first infall, before substantial orbital evolution or phase mixing. Their relative velocities closely trace the halo mass, especially when the pair separation is near the halo virial radius. In the TNG100 simulation, we find that dynamical mass estimators can recover halo masses with an intrinsic scatter of $\sim$0.2 dex. We apply this method to 10 pair systems at z=6-8 with [O III] spectroscopy from the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES). We infer the stellar-to-halo mass relation while marginalizing over projection effects, measurement uncertainties, and intrinsic scatter. We find a mean halo mass of $\log\,(M_{200}/M_\odot)=11.06\pm0.21$ at $\log\,(M_{*}/M_\odot)=9$. These galaxies do not appear to inhabit unusually massive halos. Our results instead indicate a high stellar-to-halo mass ratio, corresponding to an integrated star formation efficiency of $5^{+3}_{-2}\%$, about twice the TNG100 prediction, although the current statistical significance is limited. Future observations with larger samples will tighten these constraints and directly examine whether enhanced star formation efficiency drives the overabundance of luminous galaxies at cosmic dawn.
papers.Reasons for match: This is a JADES study measuring dark matter halo masses at z~7 using galaxy pairs and [OIII] spectroscopy, directly relevant to high-redshift galaxy formation and JWST spectroscopy.
papers.Short digest: The paper measures dark matter halo masses at z~7 using galaxy-pair dynamics calibrated on TNG100, applied to 10 JADES pair systems with [OIII] spectroscopy. It infers a mean halo mass of log(M200/Msun)=11.06 at log(M*/Msun)=9 and a high integrated star formation efficiency of ~5%, about twice the TNG100 prediction. This matters for my work because it constrains the stellar-to-halo mass relation and star formation efficiency at cosmic dawn, informing interpretations of luminous high-z and compact sources.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the pair-selection criteria and [OIII] spectroscopic measurements from JADES
Check the dynamical mass estimator calibration and its intrinsic scatter from TNG100
Examine the inferred stellar-to-halo mass relation and star formation efficiency with uncertainties
Assess the projection-effect and measurement-uncertainty marginalization in the inference

papers.title: Rethinking Domain Specialization for Open-Ended Scientific Reasoning in Astronomy Language Models
papers.authors: Vanessa Lama , Sanjay Das , Emily Herron , Yuan-Sen Ting , Tijmen de Haan , Junqi Yin , Tirthankar Ghosal , Feiyi Wang
papers.subjects: Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computers and Society (cs.CY); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
papers.abstract: Domain-specialized language models are widely used for scientific question answering, but stronger general-purpose systems raise a sharper question: when does domain-specific fine-tuning remain valuable for open-ended scientific reasoning? We study this in astronomy with a curated QA benchmark from publicly available 2017--2026 Olympiad-style materials. The free-response subset contains 300 questions, including 204 text-only and 96 image-linked examples. We compare open-weight and API-served general-purpose, multimodal, and astronomy-specialized models using judge-based correctness and complementary reference metrics. Strong general-purpose models establish the highest correctness baseline in this testbed, while analyses of metric agreement, judge sensitivity, benchmark composition, and modality reveal variation not captured by a single leaderboard. These results motivate treating domain specialization as a task- and deployment-dependent property and highlight the role of domain-specific evaluation in determining which models, capabilities, and evaluation criteria are appropriate for scientific workflows.
papers.Reasons for match: This directly addresses domain-specialized astronomy language models and evaluation for open-ended scientific reasoning, which is relevant to AI-for-astronomy workflows and automated classification/inference.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks when domain-specific fine-tuning of language models remains valuable for open-ended scientific reasoning in astronomy. Using a 300-question Olympiad-style benchmark, it finds strong general-purpose and multimodal models often match or beat astronomy-specialized models, with results depending on task and modality. This matters for my work because it informs how to choose and evaluate LLMs/LMMs for astronomy tasks like AGN selection, spectral inference, and literature analysis.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the benchmark composition and whether any questions involve JWST, AGN, or galaxy classification
Check the judge-based correctness methodology and metric agreement analyses for evaluation design lessons
Examine the text-only vs image-linked modality comparison and its implications for multimodal astronomy models
Check whether they release the benchmark or code for reuse in astronomy-AI workflows

papers.title: Chandra Lensing-cluster Ultradeep Extragalactic Survey (CLUES) I: A 2 Ms Point-Source Catalog of the Abell 2744 Field
papers.authors: Shouyi Wang , Fan Zou , Elena Gallo , Bin Luo , W. N. Brandt , Yuxuan Pang , Tommaso Treu , Xue-Bing Wu , Dieu D. Nguyen , Guido Roberts-Borsani , Shengzhe Wang , Weiwei Xu , Zihao Zuo
papers.abstract: In the first paper of the Chandra Lensing-cluster Ultradeep Extragalactic Survey (CLUES), we present an ultradeep 2 Ms X-ray survey of the Abell 2744 field constructed from 101 archival Chandra ACIS-I observations. With an exposure comparable to the Chandra Deep Fields and further boosted by strong-lensing magnification from the Abell 2744 cluster at $z=0.3$, this field represents the third deepest extragalactic X-ray survey of the sky and also has rich synergy with extensive coverage by the Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope. We present the Chandra data reduction and detect sources in the soft (0.5-2 keV), hard (2-7 keV), and full (0.5-7 keV) bands over a total area of $369~\mathrm{arcmin^2}$. We perform dedicated image fitting with Chandra point spread functions to optimize point-source detections and improve X-ray positions and further screen the detections to address the impact of the central bright, structured intracluster medium. A total of 327 X-ray point sources are detected and cataloged, including their X-ray photometry and basic spectral properties. Detailed simulations are also conducted, based on which the expected 50% flux completeness reaches $6.3\times10^{-16}$, $2.8\times10^{-16}$, and $4.9\times10^{-16}~\mathrm{erg~cm^{-2}~s^{-1}}$ in the full, soft, and hard bands, respectively. The source number density as a function of flux is consistent with those in blank-field surveys within a factor of $\approx2$, with a slight excess above $\approx10^{-14}~\mathrm{erg~cm^{-2}~s^{-1}}$. All X-ray data products are publicly released, including the catalog, X-ray images, exposure maps, background maps, and sensitivity maps.
papers.Reasons for match: This is an ultradeep Chandra X-ray survey in the Abell 2744 field with strong JWST/HST synergy, relevant to AGN selection and high-redshift X-ray source studies.
papers.Short digest: CLUES presents a 2 Ms Chandra point-source catalog of the Abell 2744 field, one of the deepest extragalactic X-ray surveys with lensing magnification and JWST synergy. It catalogs 327 X-ray point sources with photometry and spectral properties and releases all data products publicly. This matters for my work because X-ray AGN catalogs in JWST deep fields help identify and classify obscured/broad-line AGN and cross-match with LRD and compact-red-source samples.
Full-text inspection checklist: Check the X-ray source catalog for counterparts and redshift information relevant to high-z AGN
Look for the sensitivity/completeness maps to assess detectability of faint high-z AGN
Examine whether any sources overlap with known JWST LRD or compact-red-source samples
Assess the spectral fitting diagnostics that separate AGN from star-forming X-ray emission

papers.title: Resolving 3 Exotic Hyperbolic-Umbilic Lensing Configurations in the "Cosmic Mantis": An Exploration of RXJ0437.1+0043 with JWST
papers.authors: Catherine Cerny , David J. Lagattuta , Keren Sharon , Gourav Khullar , Benjamin Beauchesne , Alastair C. Edge , Mathilde Jauzac , Marceau Limousin , Guillaume Mahler , Lukas J. Furtak , Leo Fung , Qiuhan He , Richard J. Massey , Ashish K. Meena , Adi Zitrin
papers.abstract: We present an updated strong lensing model for the galaxy cluster RXJ0437.1+0043 (z=0.285) using new JWST NIRCam imaging in four pass-bands. The cluster field notably displays at least three separate gravitationally lensed galaxies in hyperbolic-umbilic (H-U) configurations, which in the JWST imaging show exquisitely resolved stellar clumps at scales as small as 0.04''. We identify 13 new systems of multiply-imaged lensed galaxies and determine the redshifts for two sources based on archival spectroscopic observations. We also identify over 50 individually resolved substructure clumps in the multiple images of eight galaxies and add them into the lens model, for a total of 275 positional lensing constraints between all 26 lensed sources used in the model. We investigate the impact of different modeling choices on our results. In the final lens model, we reproduce the observed multiple images with a precision of 0.23'' , and achieve 0.13'' specifically for the H-U systems. We estimate a total enclosed mass in the cluster's strong lensing regime of M(<110 kpc) ~ 8.2 x 10^13 Msun, reconstruct the source images of the most highly magnified galaxies, and measure time delays in the most magnified, morphologically detailed systems. The isotropic lensing effect from the H-U configurations enables future detailed studies of the properties of their source galaxies, and the number and spatial density of additional constraints improve the model's ability to detect dark matter substructures within the cluster core.
papers.Reasons for match: This is a JWST NIRCam strong-lensing study of a galaxy cluster, relevant to JWST deep-field imaging and high-redshift source reconstruction, though not directly about LRDs or AGN. It may still be useful for lensing-assisted studies of faint high-z sources.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks how to model the complex strong-lensing field of RXJ0437.1+0043 using new JWST NIRCam imaging. It identifies 13 new multiply-imaged systems, resolves many stellar clumps, and improves the lens model precision, especially for hyperbolic-umbilic configurations. For my work, the paper matters as a JWST imaging and lens-modeling resource that could enable magnified studies of high-redshift galaxies and possibly faint AGN.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for the redshift distribution of lensed sources and whether any are at cosmic dawn
Check whether the source reconstructions reveal compact red sources or AGN-like clumps
Assess the lens-model uncertainties and whether they are small enough for high-z source SED or morphology studies
Look for any mention of follow-up spectroscopy or multi-band SED fitting of the lensed sources

papers.title: Toward Autonomous Radio Follow-up of Multi-messenger Transients with RADAR: From Alert Parsing to Inference and Observation Scheduling
papers.authors: Mihael Hategan-Marandiuc , Tanner O'Dwyer , Alessandra Corsi , Eliu Huerta , Zilinghan Li , Ian T. Foster , Kyle Chard , Ryan Chard , Amal Gueroudji
papers.subjects: High Energy Astrophysical Phenomena (astro-ph.HE) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: Multi-messenger astronomy (MMA), the joint study of cosmic sources through gravitational waves (GWs), electromagnetic (EM) radiation, neutrinos, and cosmic rays, is rapidly reshaping time-domain astrophysics. Realizing the promise of MMA will require coordinating heterogeneous observing resources and automating the chain from alert to analysis to follow-up. RADAR (Radio Afterglow Detection and AI-driven Response) is a federated, privacy-enhancing framework for the radio follow-up of GW events, previously validated on GW170817. Here, we extend it along three axes. First, we benchmark three large language models (LLMs; GPT-5.5, Claude-Opus-4.7, and Gemini-3.5-Flash) against the GW170817 radio light curve dataset. GPT-5.5 attains the highest event-level $F_1$ score, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, at $0.893 \pm 0.010$, and the highest GCN-level recall, $0.794 \pm 0.013$, improving on previous GPT-4.1 results by 16\% and 10\%, respectively, while Claude-Opus-4.7 achieves the highest precision, $0.978 \pm 0.014$. Second, we introduce concurrent likelihood evaluation, which speeds up the MCMC computation by a factor of $40\times$ over our previous results. Third, we present an LLM-driven scheme that converts natural-language observing requests into submission-ready scheduling blocks for the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. Together, these developments advance RADAR toward a scalable, largely autonomous system for GW radio follow up.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper applies LLMs and automated scheduling to multi-messenger radio follow-up, which connects to my interest in AI/LLMs for astronomy workflows, though it is not about JWST, high-z galaxies, or AGN. It is relevant as an AI-for-astronomy methods paper.
papers.Short digest: The paper asks how to automate the chain from gravitational-wave alert parsing to radio follow-up inference and observation scheduling using the RADAR framework. It benchmarks three LLMs on the GW170817 radio light-curve dataset, reports improved event-level F1 and recall for GPT-5.5, introduces concurrent likelihood evaluation speeding MCMC by 40x, and presents an LLM-driven scheme converting natural-language observing requests into VLA scheduling blocks. For my work, it is a useful example of LLM-driven automation and agentic workflows in astronomy, even if the science target is not high-z JWST.
Full-text inspection checklist: Look for details on how LLM outputs are validated against physical models and whether hallucination/uncertainty is controlled
Check the alert-parsing and scheduling pipeline architecture for transferable ideas to JWST/AGN follow-up automation
Assess whether the benchmarking metrics and datasets are reproducible or extensible to other transient/AGN classes

Title: Toward Autonomous Radio Follow-up of Multi-messenger Transients with RADAR: From Alert Parsing to Inference and Observation Scheduling
Authors: Mihael Hategan-Marandiuc , Tanner O'Dwyer , Alessandra Corsi , Eliu Huerta , Zilinghan Li , Ian T. Foster , Kyle Chard , Ryan Chard , Amal Gueroudji
Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18233
Relevancy score: 6
Reasons for match: This paper applies LLMs and automated scheduling to multi-messenger radio follow-up, which connects to my interest in AI/LLMs for astronomy workflows, though it is not about JWST, high-z galaxies, or AGN. It is relevant as an AI-for-astronomy methods paper.
Short digest: The paper asks how to automate the chain from gravitational-wave alert parsing to radio follow-up inference and observation scheduling using the RADAR framework. It benchmarks three LLMs on the GW170817 radio light-curve dataset, reports improved event-level F1 and recall for GPT-5.5, introduces concurrent likelihood evaluation speeding MCMC by 40x, and presents an LLM-driven scheme converting natural-language observing requests into VLA scheduling blocks. For my work, it is a useful example of LLM-driven automation and agentic workflows in astronomy, even if the science target is not high-z JWST.
Full-text inspection checklist: ['Look for details on how LLM outputs are validated against physical models and whether hallucination/uncertainty is controlled', 'Check the alert-parsing and scheduling pipeline architecture for transferable ideas to JWST/AGN follow-up automation', 'Assess whether the benchmarking metrics and datasets are reproducible or extensible to other transient/AGN classes']
